Amory lay awake in the dormitory and listened to the other boys breathing. It was midnight, and the radiators knocked softly in the dark. He had been at the school for six weeks and still felt like a visitor, someone who had wandered into a house by mistake and been too polite to leave. At home he had been clever; here, clever was ordinary, and he was uncertain what else he had to offer. He turned over and stared at the ceiling. “I will be somebody,” he thought, with a vagueness that embarrassed him even as he thought it, and then, because nothing else came, he closed his eyes and waited for morning.
